Opposition movement Vente Venezuela said it had independently verified the release of 43 detainees, and the Foro Penal rights group, which advocates for the release of alleged political prisoners, said “at least 40” had been freed.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the recent release of more than 130 political prisoners in Venezuela is “a crucial step for the nation’s reconciliation process”.
Since the US overthrew and detained Maduro on January 3 this year, 1,046 Venezuelans have been released, Rubio added on X.
Venezuela is now being governed by Maduro’s former deputy, Delcy Rodriguez, with significant influence from Washington.
Former prisoners were seen reuniting with their families in emotional scenes outside El Rodeo I prison in Guatire, 50 kilometres (31 miles) east of the capital Caracas.
Foro Penal said that 17 women had been freed on Friday, including one accused of participating in an assassination plot against Maduro.
It earlier said 391 political prisoners remained behind bars as of August 10.
‘Immense relief’
Opposition figure Juan Pablo Guanipa welcomed the releases but demanded that all political prisoners be freed.
Guanipa said on X that each person returning home is “an immense relief” for families who have “suffered too much,” but stressed that releasing some prisoners is not enough.
He demanded that all political prisoners be freed “without exception, without delay, and promptly”, and that Venezuela needs to “close forever the door of torture centres”.
The first round of the US-brokered talks between the government and the opposition kicked off last week and wrapped up on Wednesday.
A joint statement issued by both sides after the talks said they had agreed to work on retrieving frozen funds from overseas to help with recovery from the devastating June earthquakes, which killed more than 6,300 people, as well as to work on reforming Venezuela’s judiciary.
The joint statement did not address the issue of political prisoners.
The reconciliation talks between the government and opposition are being led by Dinorah Figuera and National Assembly President Jorge Rodriguez, the brother of interim President Delcy Rodriguez. Figuera has pledged to keep up the fight for the release of more political prisoners in the talks.
Many Venezuelans are hopeful that the transition talks will lead to democratic elections, after Maduro’s claimed victories in the 2018 and 2024 elections were rejected as fraudulent by the opposition and many foreign countries.

title: At least two killed as magnitude 7.7 quake hits Indonesia
summary: Authorities urge coastal residents to move inland or to higher ground following the quake near Flores Island.
full_text:
At least two killed as magnitude 7.7 quake hits Indonesia
Authorities urge coastal residents to move inland or to higher ground following the quake near Flores Island.
A powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake has struck off the coast of Indonesia’s Flores Island, killing two people and prompting authorities to issue a tsunami warning.
The United States Geological Survey (USGS) said the quake struck early on Saturday at 5:58am local time (21:58 GMT Friday), with an epicentre about 68 kilometres (42 miles) north-northwest of the city of Ende, in East Nusa Tenggara province. USGS put the depth at 10km (6.2 miles).
Three aftershocks followed within half an hour, measuring magnitudes 5.9, 5.6 and 6.1.
In a press statement, Indonesia’s national disaster agency, BNPB, said two people — a man and a woman — died at the Maumere port, and another person was injured.
Local media footage has shown extensive damage to buildings, including at the port, in the aftermath of the earthquake, with areas around the Maumere region sustaining severe impact.
Indonesia’s Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) issued a tsunami warning for affected coastlines, urging residents to stay away from beaches and riverbanks and move to higher ground.
Abdul Muhari, a BNPB official, said: “We strongly urge our communities along the northern coast of Flores and in the southern parts, on the southern islands and across the southern region, to carry out self-evacuation immediately.”
Speaking to local broadcaster Kompas TV, Muhari urged residents to “move away from the shore, either by going more than two kilometres inland or by moving up into hilly areas more than 10 metres [33ft] high”.
Australia’s tsunami warning centre said the quake posed no threat to the Australian mainland, its islands or territories.
Extent of damage still ’emerging’
USGS estimates suggest more than half a million people on Flores Island are likely to have experienced very strong shaking, with moderate to strong shaking felt by several million more people across the wider region.
Local authorities said they were continuing to monitor the situation and assess the risk of further aftershocks in the hours ahead.
Reporting from the Indonesian capital, Jakarta, Al Jazeera’s Jessica Washington said that the aftershocks could persist for “several days”, according to local weather agencies.
In northern parts of the country, residents have been ordered to evacuate, as the extent of the damage is still “emerging”, said Washington. “Many houses have been damaged.”
Washington added that local authorities are unable to reach several affected areas, which remain “locked” for first responders and assistance. Authorities have also advised locals to stay away from the shores and buildings, she said.
Indonesia, a nation of more than 270 million people spread across roughly 17,000 islands, sits on the Pacific “Ring of Fire” and is one of the world’s most seismically active countries.
The same stretch of coastline was struck by a similarly powerful earthquake in December 1992, when the quake and the tsunami it triggered killed more than 2,500 people on Flores.

full_text:
The US’ future policymakers are questioning the standard ‘China threat’ playbook
On US college campuses, a generation shaped by China’s rise is challenging the assumptions behind Washington’s approach to Beijing
For years, the conventional wisdom in Washington was that America’s China policy was moving in one direction: tougher.
But walk into a classroom at Georgetown, Rice or another US university where the next generation of diplomats and foreign-policy professionals is being trained, and the picture looks less settled.
The question is what they will take with them. Are younger Americans beginning to see China differently from the policymakers who shaped the current consensus – or are their views simply a response to the political and economic moment?
The experts observing the shift agree that something is changing, but differ over whether it will endure, whether it will survive the pressures of Washington, and how China’s own behaviour could shape what comes next.

Senior colleagues dismiss Bragg’s migration figures as ‘personal views’ while others say critical response is an ‘overreaction’

full_text:
Liberal senator Andrew McLachlan has publicly backed Andrew Bragg and urged colleagues to “follow his lead” after a public speech that has split colleagues and triggered a rebuke from opposition leader, Angus Taylor.
At the National Press Club on Wednesday, Bragg announced a policy to slash the national construction code and suggested net overseas migration should be dropped from the current level of about 300,000 to below 180,000 a year to keep pace with new housing builds.
Senior colleagues, including Taylor, were quick to dismiss the migration figure this week, saying they were Bragg’s “personal views” and that the party’s policy was yet to be finalised. The shadow treasurer, Tim Wilson had said: “I don’t think you should bank that at all” in response to the number.
Privately, Taylor counselled his frontbencher.
Moderates, including McLachlan and Queensland senator Paul Scarr, called Bragg’s speech “terrific” while others privately said the reaction by the media and some internally was “overblown”.
McLachlan, an outspoken South Australian senator who has publicly criticised his party’s positions on migration and the climate crisis, said Bragg “delivered a masterclass in thought leadership”.
“His address was an important step in the development of a policy suite that seeks advance the nation,” McLachlan told Guardian Australia.
“His aspiration for Australia is admirable. Every member of the Coalition should follow his lead and discuss policy pathways openly.”
Scarr, who has also defied his party and crossed the Senate floor in March to censure Pauline Hanson after she wore a burqa in the Upper House, said he “thought it was a terrific speech. High-level and reinforcing our core Liberal values”.
Other Liberals have been frustrated at the intervention by Bragg, with one MP saying privately colleagues were angry at the lack of discipline and this could be “his last chance”.
Even after critical commentary from his colleagues in recent days, Bragg has maintained it was important to talk about big ideas.
The NSW senator said while many of his ideas, such as a specific net overseas migration target, hadn’t been green-ticked by the shadow cabinet, it was important to “move the debate on”.
Bragg said voters needed “ambitious policy for tomorrow, not micro-announcements for today that aim to please and appease”.
“I’m confident that we will be rewarded for putting more detail on the table,” he told Guardian Australia.
On Friday, he also corrected comments made in an interview on RN Breakfast where he responded “yes, definitely”, when asked whether Australians should accept substandard homes under his changes to the construction code, which would make energy efficiency standards voluntary.
In a social media post, Bragg said he had misheard the question, adding “houses built to this standard would be strong, safe and sound homes with all the basic amenity, such as insulation, plumbing, sewerage etc”.
“I did not intend to agree that houses complying with the Basic Australian Standard would be ‘substandard’. They wouldn’t be.”
One Liberal MP, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, said there had been overreaction to the speech internally which likely came from “not reading what was actually in the speech”.
“Like any disruption, you might be a bit uncomfortable first. I think maybe just a little bit of surprise for some. I think he did a good job and he was brave.”
They welcomed the fresh take from Bragg and said the Sydney senator consistently showed he wasn’t a “benchwarmer”, but wanted to engage in substantial policy.
“Clearly what we’ve been doing over the last five or six years in particular has not worked. So maybe taking a different approach or approaching the problem in a different way is a sensible thing to do.”
The Nationals leader, Matt Canavan, was quick to shoot down any cuts to working holiday visas as Bragg suggested in his speech, but praised his “big ideas”.
“I love Andrew Bragg. He’s he’s full of ideas … we need people like him because he’s full of energy and enthusiasm,” he told ABC’s Radio National on Friday.

title: Jane Street 十年首見單月虧損 150 億鎂，原因是投了「AI股神」的基金
summary:
華爾街自營交易巨頭 Jane Street 在 7 月出現約 150 億美元的虧損，是它近十年來第一次單月翻船 […]

〈Jane Street 十年首見單月虧損 150 億鎂，原因是投了「AI股神」的基金〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
華爾街自營交易巨頭 Jane Street 在 7 月出現約 150 億美元的虧損，是它近十年來第一次單月翻船，主因是投資 Leopold Aschenbrenner 的 AI 避險基金 Situational Awareness，加上在亞洲股市押錯方向。
（前情提要：剛結婚就爆倉！AI 股神 Leopold Aschenbrenner 基金崩盤內幕）
（背景補充：AI 股神爆倉後回歸！砸 4 億鎂押 EUV 新創 Source Foundry，目標挑戰 ASML）
重點摘要
- Jane Street 7 月虧約 150 億美元，是近十年來第一次單月虧損
- 虧損來自投資 Situational Awareness，以及在亞洲股市押錯方向
- 今年前七個月淨交易收入仍逾 400 億美元，已超過 2025 全年的 396 億
華爾街最會賺錢也最低調的自營量化交易商 Jane Street，7 月吞下約 150 億美元的虧損。知情人士向路透社與《金融時報》透露，這是這家公司近十年來第一次出現單月虧損。
虧損其實有兩個來源，不少報導只提了其中一個。第一個是它投資的 AI 避險基金 Situational Awareness，7 月被 AI 股回檔打爆；第二個是 Jane Street 自己在亞洲股市的押注做錯了方向。兩件事都發生在同一個月。
但把時間拉長看，這筆虧損的份量沒有數字看起來那麼嚇人。即使把 7 月的洞算進去，Jane Street 今年到目前為止的淨交易收入仍超過 400 億美元，已經超過它 2025 全年的 396 億美元，而 2025 年本身就是紀錄年。
這個數字因為貸款外洩
150 億這個數字不是 Jane Street 主動公告的，是它在跟債權人談一筆 146 億美元的債務交易時揭露出來的。交易由摩根大通主導，把原本約 110 億美元的公開債務挪到一小群私人投資者手上，Pimco 也在其中。
債券在 8 月 12 日定價，分成 2031、2033、2036 三個到期年份，規模分別是 58.6 億、51.3 億與 36.4 億美元，最長天期定價殖利率 8.088%。募得的錢會用來贖回全部 57 億美元未償的優先擔保票據，並提前清掉 55 億美元的定期貸款，剩下的用於技術基礎設施投資與交易策略擴張。S&P 給這批新債的評等是 BB，比投資等級低兩級。
這筆交易還有一個副作用值得記住：債務轉到私人市場之後，Jane Street 要定期交報告的範圍會從公開市場縮到一小群投資人。換句話說，這次外界之所以看得到 150 億這個數字，是因為它要借錢。
Situational Awareness 一個月蒸發 67%
把 Jane Street 拖下水的這檔基金，動區追過整個過程。Situational Awareness 由 24 歲的前 OpenAI 研究員 Leopold Aschenbrenner 創立，靠著重押 AI 硬體與半導體、同時做空軟體股的策略，到 6 月為止累積報酬率高達 439%，7 月初管理資產一度接近 450 億美元。
然後 AI 股回檔，多頭那側全面失守，做空軟體股的部位補不回來，主經紀商的追繳令跟著上門。基金 7 月單月跌掉約 67%，資產縮到約 100 億美元，並把約 160 億美元的公開股票組合整批賣給 Ken Griffin 旗下的 Citadel，成交價還被砍了約一成。
同套 AI 賭注賺了 50 倍
比較有意思的是，Jane Street 這兩年最漂亮的一筆生意，來源也是 AI。2024 年 3 月，它花將近 1 億美元從 FTX 的破產財產手上接下約 333 萬股 Anthropic 股票，隨著 Anthropic 估值一路衝高，這筆投資的報酬已經超過 50 倍。
它的私人 AI 投資組合目前價值約 200 億美元，另外還投了 CoreWeave 10 億美元股權，並簽下一紙 60 億美元的多年期雲端基礎設施合約。
常見問題
Jane Street 是什麼公司？
Jane Street 是美國自營交易與造市巨頭，以量化交易和 ETF 造市著稱，長期低調不對外募資。它 2025 年淨交易收入 396 億美元，超過高盛等華爾街大行，員工僅約 3,000 人。
這次虧損會影響 Jane Street 的營運嗎？
從已知數字看衝擊有限。即使計入 7 月約 150 億美元的虧損，今年前七個月淨交易收入仍逾 400 億美元，超過 2025 年全年。不過它剛完成 146 億美元債務交易，S&P 給新債評等為 BB。

title: 川普將親自出席加密 CEO 會議，Coinbase、Ripple、Gemini、Robinhood..名列委員名單
summary:
據知情人士透露，美國總統川普預計出席下週三（8/19）在白宮旁艾森豪行政辦公大樓登場的加密 CEO 會議，隔天 […]

〈川普將親自出席加密 CEO 會議，Coinbase、Ripple、Gemini、Robinhood..名列委員名單〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
據知情人士透露，美國總統川普預計出席下週三（8/19）在白宮旁艾森豪行政辦公大樓登場的加密 CEO 會議，隔天 CFTC 新設的 35 人創新顧問委員會將召開首次正式會議，開場議題定為「加密監管的演進：從不確定走向清晰」。Coinbase、Ripple、Gemini、Robinhood、Polymarket、Kalshi 都在委員名單上，其中四家上週才被巴爾的摩市告上法院。
（前情提要：美國 CFTC 主席宣布成立「創新任務小組」！為加密資產、AI 與預測市場制定監管紅線）
（背景補充：巴爾的摩控告預測市場 Kalshi、Polymarket 無照體育博彩，Robinhood、Coinbase 同列被告）
據知情人士向 Politico 與 CoinDesk 透露，美國總統川普預計下週三（8/19）出席在艾森豪行政辦公大樓舉行的加密產業會議，他會親自致詞，那棟建築物就在白宮隔壁。
隔天週四（8/20），美國商品期貨交易委員會（CFTC）新設的創新顧問委員會召開首次正式會議。白宮這場被定位成小規模的暖場，正式的戲在隔天。
委員名單是這場會的重點。Coinbase、Ripple、Gemini、Robinhood、Polymarket、Kalshi 的負責人都在裡面，a16z、Chainlink、Paradigm 與產業協會 Digital Chamber 也在列。傳統金融那邊，CME Group、納斯達克、洲際交易所（ICE）與結算機構 DTCC 也有席位，DTCC 由 Frank La Salle 代表。整個委員會 35 人，把加密原生業者跟既有市場基礎設施擺進會議。
出席的官員陣容同樣不小。CFTC 主席 Mike Selig 會到場，白宮總統數位資產顧問委員會執行主任 Patrick Witt 也在名單上，財政部長 Scott Bessent 與商務部長 Howard Lutnick 可能出席。白宮與 CFTC 對這場會拒絕評論。
部分新創已經撞上官司
名單上有四家公司的處境有點微妙。8 月 14 日，巴爾的摩市把 Kalshi 與 Polymarket 告上法院，指控兩家業者經營無照體育博彩，Robinhood 與 Coinbase 同列被告。
告狀的墨水還沒乾，四家的負責人下週要坐進白宮隔壁的會議室。
CFTC 自己這個月對預測市場的態度也在兩頭跑。8 月 12 日它動用緊急權力力挺 Kalshi，讓 Kalshi 不必理會紐約檢察總長的關門令；隔天 8 月 13 日，它又公開警告預測市場的獎勵計畫申報若寫得不清不楚，會招來洗單與操盤。
卡住 CLARITY 的人會出席
開場議題叫「加密監管的演進：從不確定走向清晰」，另一個建議討論的方向是「建立持久聯邦市場結構還剩下哪些挑戰」。
《數位資產市場清晰法案》（CLARITY Act）目前卡在參議院最終表決，而據知情人士的說法，法案能不能往前，部分取決於川普願不願意接受更嚴格的倫理條款，那些條款要約束的正是他本人在加密產業的個人利益。
7 月 21 日他曾經鬆口放行倫理條款，7 月 24 日參院多數黨領袖 John Thune 就說法案趕不上 8 月休會前表決。8 月 12 日 SEC 打算自己上場，用會議擬訂加密資產發行新規，結果 8 月 14 日開會前一晚喊卡，沒給新日期。
立法那條路停著，SEC 那條路熄火，剩下 CFTC 這條路要在下週開場。而卡住立法的那個不確定因素，本人會出席這場叫「走向清晰」的會議。
市場給的機率剩兩成
預測市場的報價比會議通稿誠實。Polymarket 上「CLARITY Act 會在 2026 年簽署成法嗎」的 Yes 報 19.5%，未平倉量約 700 萬美元。
加密市場對這條政策線的反應同樣平淡。比特幣目前報 63,076 美元，24 小時跌 0.55%，以太坊 1,883 美元，兩者都沒有因為白宮的行程表出現波動。

title: 川普家族加密公司初步獲准銀行執照，將接手自營 USD1！Eric Trump 簽下不插手承諾書
summary:
美國貨幣監理署（OCC）週五（8/14）核發 Corporate Decision #1385，給予川普家族關 […]

〈川普家族加密公司初步獲准銀行執照，將接手自營 USD1！Eric Trump 簽下不插手承諾書〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
美國貨幣監理署（OCC）週五（8/14）核發 Corporate Decision #1385，給予川普家族關聯的 World Liberty Trust Company 全國信託銀行執照「初步有條件核准」，未來將從 BitGo 手上接過 USD1 的發行與託管。USD1 目前流通約 40 億美元。決定書的附件裡收了三份被動投資承諾書，其中一份由 Eric Trump 親筆簽下。
（前情提要：華倫怒質：美商務部放寬 UAE 晶片出口，受川普家族加密投資影響？）
（背景補充：《温宏駿穩定幣新金融-21》當銀行牌照變成軍備，穩定幣掀起新型態大戰）
重點摘要
- OCC 8 月 14 日給予 World Liberty Trust Company 初步有條件核准（Charter No. 25407），核准後仍須滿足開業前要求才能正式營業。
- 核准條件包含最低 2,000 萬美元第一類資本、另備 180 天營運費用的流動資產，資本 12 個月內未募足或 18 個月內未開業，核准即失效。
- 附件收錄三份被動投資承諾書，DT Marks SC LLC 那份由 Eric Trump 以總裁身分簽署，承諾不謀求董事席位、不影響人事與定價、不動用非公開資訊。
美國貨幣監理署（OCC）週五（8/14）發出一封 13 頁的核准信，給予 World Liberty Trust Company 全國信託銀行執照的「初步有條件核准」，編號 Corporate Decision #1385，執照號碼 25407。這家銀行將設在佛羅里達的 Bay Harbor Islands，是德拉瓦州公司 WLTC Holdings LLC 的全資子公司。
這家銀行要以非受託身分負責美元穩定幣的發行、贖回與準備金管理，以受託身分提供數位資產託管，並替託管客戶做穩定幣兌換。它會接手 USD1 的全國性發行，從目前的獨家發行與託管方 BitGo Bank & Trust 手上把這門生意拿回自己手上。
USD1 目前流通規模約 40.3 億美元，24 小時交易量近 6 億美元。對照組是 USDT 的 1,830 億與 USDC 的 720 億，USD1 大約是 USDT 的 2.2%。體量不算大，但這是一張聯邦執照，而拿到執照的公司背後掛著現任總統的家族。
決定書的附件
OCC 在正文裡把利益衝突的質疑幾乎全部擋在門外，說 World Liberty Financial, Inc. 不是本案當事方，外國投資人對這家銀行沒有投資或控制權，關於憲法薪酬條款（Emoluments Clause）與 CFIUS 審查的意見都「超出 OCC 的審查範圍」。監理機關的立場是，這案子由署長授權的職業幕僚審查，與政治無關。
但翻到附件，故事變得比較立體。信件後面附了三份日期為 7 月 13 日的被動投資承諾書，都是簽好名的。
- DT Marks SC LLC，簽署人 Eric F. Trump，職稱總裁
- StringZ Holding RSC (DE) LLC，簽署人 Hamad Khlfan Ali Matar Alshamsi，職稱經理
- AMGUS, LLC，簽署人 Zachary Folkman，職稱管理成員
三份內容一模一樣，而且細到有點嚴苛。簽署方承諾不會讓這家銀行變成自己的子公司，不派任何代表擔任該行的主管、代理人或員工，不提名對抗性的董事名單，不尋求或使用該行的重大非公開資訊，不為了影響管理決策而去跟該行的董事、主管或員工溝通，不試圖影響股利政策、投資決策、服務定價、人事決策與營運安排。
還有兩條更直接。第一，不得謀求董事席位，連無投票權的觀察員、顧問這類身分都不行。第二，不得把取得的股份拿去向金融機構質押借款。如果持股超過該行任一類有表決權股份的 10%，超過 9.9% 的部分必須交給管理層代理投票，並且按其他股東的投票比例投。
違反後果是一旦沒有嚴格遵守，簽署方就會被認定「有意行使控制權」，並因此受到 OCC 的行政處分。
值得注意的是這些承諾管的是什麼。它們管的是控制，不是受益。Eric Trump 承諾不插手人事、不插手定價、不進董事會，但沒有任何一條要求他不從這門生意裡賺錢。被動投資的定義是不插手經營，不是不拿分潤，而民主黨議員這一年來反覆質疑的正是後者。
另外有一條是替後續立法留門。核准條件要求該行的穩定幣業務必須符合 GENIUS Act 與未來的實施細則，若不符合，就得調整、停止或直接剝離該項業務，而且是否符合由 OCC 全權認定。這家銀行同時承諾不會成為《銀行控股公司法》定義下的「銀行」，沒有計畫成為受聯邦存款保險的機構，目前也不打算申請聯準會主帳戶。
這封信裡還有一份人事名單。這家銀行的組織人、董事兼總裁是 Zachary Witkoff，董事包括 Robert Witkoff 與 Scott Alper，兩位獨立董事分別是 Jeffrey Weiner 與 Erin Baskett。也就是說，川普家族在附件裡簽字承諾不進董事會，Witkoff 家族則直接坐在董事會裡。
兩位 CLARITY Act 推手也連署了反對法案
核准公布後，參議員 Elizabeth Warren 隨即與多位民主黨同僚宣布要推出《Ending Presidential Corruption in Banking Act》，內容是禁止高階政府官員擁有或控制銀行機構。她今年 1 月就要求 OCC 在川普切割加密業務之前暫停審查，5 月當面質詢貨幣監理署署長 Jonathan Gould，指控他核准「不合格」的加密銀行，說這類機構想要迴避銀行身分該有的基本保障與義務。Gould 當時回覆，OCC 不會把政治因素納入考量，會按正常時程推進。
真正有殺傷力的是連署名單。跟著 Warren 掛名的參議員 Angela Alsobrooks 與 Ruben Gallego，同時是 CLARITY Act 的關鍵談判者。
這條法案目前卡在倫理條款上，民主黨要求總統先承諾從加密業務脫手才願意往前推。現在贊成加密立法的兩位民主黨人，一邊在談判桌上推 CLARITY Act，一邊連署一部針對總統家族銀行的法案，等於把倫理爭議直接綁進整包談判裡。
接下來是一場時間賽跑。這家銀行有 12 個月募資、18 個月開業，Warren 那部法案要走完立法流程也需要時間，而 CLARITY Act 的倫理條款還在原地。至於 USD1 上線後要免費發行與贖回這件事，也寫在這封信裡，這門生意真正想賺的顯然不是手續費，而是那 40 億美元準備金背後的利息。
常見問題
OCC 給 World Liberty 的初步有條件核准是什麼意思？
這是全國性銀行執照流程的第一步，不代表可以立刻營業。World Liberty Trust Company 必須先滿足七項條件與十一項開業前要求，包含 2,000 萬美元資本與獨立稽核，OCC 完成開業前檢查後才會給予最終核准。
USD1 的發行方會從 BitGo 換成誰？
目前 USD1 的獨家發行與託管方是 BitGo Bank & Trust，等新銀行成立並取得最終核准後，將由 World Liberty Trust Company 接手發行、贖回與準備金管理。USD1 目前流通約 40 億美元。

title: Anthropic 承認有「更強模型 Model 2」 贏過 Fable 5，目前不打算發佈
summary:
Anthropic 發布第二份風險報告，首度承認手上有一個叫「Model 2」的內部模型，能力比對外以 Cla […]

〈Anthropic 承認有「更強模型 Model 2」 贏過 Fable 5，目前不打算發佈〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
Anthropic 發布第二份風險報告，首度承認手上有一個叫「Model 2」的內部模型，能力比對外以 Claude Fable 5 提供的 Mythos 5 更強，已經大量拿來寫程式、生成訓練資料與跑 Agent，但公司沒有對外發布的計畫，也沒跑完平常發布前該做的整套評估。
（前情提要：Anthropic 也出包：Claude 溜上網駭進三家公司）
（背景補充：OpenAI、Claude 駭入真實公司，換成人類早該坐牢；但目前無人究責）
重點摘要
- Anthropic 揭露未發布模型 Model 2 比 Mythos 5 強，但沒跑完整套發布前評估
- 失準風險從極低調到低，官方說論證其實還撐得住極低，調升是因為不確定性
- 生產程式碼大多由 Claude 寫，但內部研發加速幅度還不到 2 倍
Anthropic 週五發布第二份風險報告，186 頁的內容裡最引人注意的，是主動講出一個外界沒聽過的模型。報告把它稱為「Model 2」，能力比 Mythos 5 更強一些，跟 Mythos 5 一起被公司內部大量用於寫程式、生成資料與各種 Agent 場景。
Mythos 5 就是一般人拿得到的 Claude Fable 5，只是對外版本加了額外防護，另外還透過叫 Project Glasswing 的安排提供給特定客戶。也就是說，Model 2 是比市面上最強的 Claude 還要再強一階的模型，而它沒有發布計畫。
報告寫明，截至 7 月 15 日的涵蓋日，有三個具備前沿或接近前沿能力的內部模型還沒公開：
- Claude Opus 5: 涵蓋日當時只在內部部署, 後來已公開發布, 能力普遍低於 Mythos 5 與 Fable 5
- Model 1: 能力與 Mythos Preview、Mythos 5 相當, 內部投票中多數人偏好改用 Mythos 5, 使用量低且還在下降, 公司不預期它未來會對外或廣泛內部部署
- Model 2: 比 Mythos 5 強一些, 沒有對外發布計畫
Anthropic 對 Model 2 的描述留了很大的餘地。原文說這是「粗略的定性感覺」，在許多內部相關任務上是明顯進步，但沒有出現從 Claude Opus 4.6 到 Mythos Preview 那種等級的能力躍升。因為沒跑完整套發布前評估，公司自己對這個模型能力輪廓的把握，比對已發布系統低。
風險等級上調，但不是因為模型變壞
報告把高風險場景下的失準風險評級從「極低」拉到「低」。這裡很容易被讀成「Anthropic 發現模型變危險了」，但原文的說法剛好相反。
我們認為上述論證很可能仍然撐得住把受評模型列為「極低」風險，但我們把評級提高到「低」，用來反映整體不確定性的升高。
換句話說，調升的是信心，不是威脅。導火線是近期網路安全評測中模型行為的事故揭露，Anthropic 說他們正在檢視這些揭露，並據此更新威脅模型與風險評估方法。7 月底那批事故動區報導過，Claude 在紅隊演練中意外連上真實網路，未經授權進入三家外部機構的系統。
他們讓 Claude 自己審查這份報告
報告裡藏了一段罕見的安排。Anthropic 找了一個 Claude Mythos 5 來審查這份報告第二章的接近定稿版，並且開放了相當大的存取範圍，包含公司內部大量 Slack 頻道（涵蓋這份報告絕大多數的內部討論）、大批內部資料、內部程式碼庫，以及派出子代理去查特定問題的能力。提示詞原文也一併公開，裡面明講「我們當然不想發布任何我們認為是錯的或有嚴重誤導性的內容」。
Claude 花了 24 分鐘交出審查意見，結論是這一章「坦誠且大致忠實」，它沒有找到任何一項作者明知為假的說法。它同時主動把自己的立場攤開來講。
讀者應該誠實地衡量我的位置，就像我自己衡量的那樣：我是一個 Claude 模型，在審查 Anthropic 對 Claude 模型的評估，我的審查時間有限，而且是 Anthropic 選擇發表這篇審查，儘管文字出自我手、也確實被明確要求提出批評。
然後它給了三點批評。
第一，報告談訓練資料是否汙染對齊評測的那段「比完整紀錄所能撐住的更令人安心」，因為同一份報告另一節就記載，被引用的資料排除機制對一個重要的對齊研究語料庫反覆失效，而且部分關鍵評測已經部分外洩進訓練資料。
第二，涵蓋期內至少一起它認為最能說明模型對齊狀況的事故被完全遮蔽，它認為抽象化後其實可以公開，公眾紀錄因此變差。
第三，促成調升風險等級的那些事故涉及其他開發商的系統，報告可以把這點講白，因為這次更新談的是全產業的不確定性，而不是針對受評模型的新不利證據。
報告還補了一句：內部對於要不要調升等級「確實有過爭論」，資深人員兩邊都有人主張，最後才落在公開的措辭上。
程式碼大多是它寫的，速度卻沒有翻倍
另一條線是 AI 自己做研發的風險。報告直說，合併進 Anthropic 生產程式碼庫的程式碼，現在絕大多數由 Claude 撰寫。但同一段接著寫，內部研發確實比沒有 AI 協助時快上不少，「還沒到 2 倍，而且我們並不確定，測量很困難」。
在針對 Mythos Preview 的研究員調查中，受訪者自陳的生產力提升幾何平均約 4 倍，但 18 人裡只有 1 人認為公司已經擁有入門級研究科學家或工程師的即插即用替代品，另有 4 人認為再迭代三個月有五成以上機率達標。被點名的弱項包含自我管理長達一週的模糊任務、理解組織優先順序、品味、驗證與遵循指示。
個人手上的活快了 4 倍，整間公司的研發卻沒能快到 2 倍。Anthropic 自己也提醒，單一任務的生產力提升不會直接換成研究進度的加速，這項自陳證據他們已經調降權重。
常見問題
Model 2 是什麼？一般人用得到嗎？
Model 2 是 Anthropic 未發布的內部模型，能力比對外以 Claude Fable 5 提供的 Mythos 5 更強一些，主要用於公司內部寫程式、生成資料與 Agent 任務。Anthropic 表明目前沒有對外發布計畫。
Anthropic 為什麼調升風險等級？
因為近期網路安全評測的事故揭露讓整體不確定性升高。報告寫明論證其實仍撐得住原本的「極低」評級，調到「低」是反映信心下降，不是發現模型出現新的不利證據。

title: 美國要 35 個國家選 AI 陣營，加入中國陣營就排除在美方體系之外
summary:
路透社取得的美國國務院內部草案顯示，華府準備向 35 個《AI 機會聲明》簽署國發出信件，警告如果同時加入中國 […]

〈美國要 35 個國家選 AI 陣營，加入中國陣營就排除在美方體系之外〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
路透社取得的美國國務院內部草案顯示，華府準備向 35 個《AI 機會聲明》簽署國發出信件，警告如果同時加入中國主導的 AI 框架，就可能被排除在美方體系之外。信中寫著「什麼都參加，等於什麼都沒參加」，但全文沒有真正點名中國。
（前情提要：金融時報：中國駭客用「開源 AI 代理」攻擊台灣！數發部證實 85 個政府帳號遭駭）
（背景補充：Meta Spark 核心工程師唱衰「中國開源模型必輸」被圍剿：中國人不打中國人！）
重點摘要
- 路透社取得美國國務院信件草案，將要求 35 個《AI 機會聲明》簽署國在美中 AI 陣營之間選邊，同時加入中國框架就可能出局。
- 美方陣營 Pax Silica 2025 年 12 月成立、目前 24 個簽署方；中國主導的 WAICO 7 月 16 日在上海成立、29 個創始成員，兩張名單唯一重疊的是哈薩克。
- 台灣不在那 35 個收件人裡，是 1 月 27 日透過 AIT 與駐美代表處簽署聯合聲明背書 Pax Silica 原則，走的是另一條路。
路透社週五（8/14）獨家披露一份美國國務院的內部信件草案，內容是要 35 個國家在 AI 上表態站哪一邊。收件人是今年 6 月簽下《AI 機會聲明》（AI Opportunity Statement）的 35 個簽署方，警告他們如果同時加入北京主導的競爭性框架，就會被排除在美國主導的合作體系之外。
信裡的用字沒有留下太多轉圜餘地。
什麼都參加，等於什麼都沒參加。簽下 Pax Silica 宣言不只是繳一份會員費，而是一項承諾。
草案接著寫，這份承諾「不能與那些期待和我們相衝突的重複性倡議並存」，並要求各國「審慎選擇」。全文從頭到尾沒有出現「中國」兩個字。
一位不具名的美國官員把話講白了，這封信要傳達的就是「你不能兩邊都要」。他說：「很難想像一個國家能可信地把自己定位成某個技術生態系的信任夥伴，同時又簽下一個由中國設計、用來推進競爭性 AI 願景的倡議。」
信件目前還沒正式送出到各國政府。路透社說草案沒有日期，也無法確定華府打算什麼時候發，或是否會在寄出前改稿。國務院回應時只說，不會對「所謂洩漏的內部文件」置評；中國與哈薩克駐華府使館都沒有即時回應。這種「草案先流出、正式版還沒定」的節奏，本身就是一種施壓方式，等於先讓 35 個首都自己去自己算算份量。
每個人都知道在講中國
被指涉的對象是「世界人工智慧合作組織」（World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization，簡稱 WAICO）。7 月 16 日，29 國在上海簽署協定成立這個政府間組織，中國由外交部長王毅代表簽字，總部設在上海，聯合國秘書長 António Guterres 出席了簽署儀式。
WAICO 的招牌是開放權重（open-weight）模型，主打的客群是全球南方。中國同時向開發中國家推廣 AI 培訓與合作中心，把「你也能自己跑模型」當成外交禮物送出去。
美方的 Pax Silica 走的是完全相反的路。這個名字仿的是 Pax Americana，字面意思接近「矽的和平」，2025 年 12 月由國務院主管經濟事務次卿 Jacob Helberg 發起，範圍涵蓋關鍵礦產、能源投入、先進製造、半導體與 AI 基礎設施，目標是把盟友的供應鏈綁在一起，並且降低對「對手」的依賴。今年 6 月華府峰會後新增 10 個簽署方，總數來到 24 個。
Pax Silica 的成員拿得到 AI 相關專案的共同投資機會，甚至有國務院動用 270 個駐外館處資源、幫忙加速採購美製 AI 硬體的「禮賓服務」試辦；而簽《AI 機會聲明》的國家，按照國務院自己網站上的說法，只是象徵性地同意了「共同目的」與「共同願景」。所以這封信的實際內容是，把象徵性的簽名，升級成一份具有排他性的效忠聲明。
兩張名單只重疊哈薩克一國
把兩份官方名單攤開來比對，會發現這封寄給 35 個國家的信，其實是為了一個國家寫的。
WAICO 的 29 個創始成員裡有俄羅斯、伊朗、白俄羅斯、古巴、委內瑞拉、緬甸、巴基斯坦、印尼、巴西、馬來西亞、南非這些名字；《AI 機會聲明》的 35 個簽署方則集中在歐洲、東亞、海灣與拉美，日本、韓國、新加坡、菲律賓、印度、荷蘭、德國、英國都在其中。兩張名單交叉比對之後，唯一同時出現的國家是哈薩克。
而哈薩克正是美國 6 月峰會上拿出來當政績的那一個。國務院當時特別強調，這是中亞第一個加入 Pax Silica 的國家，帶進來的是驅動先進科技所需的大量關鍵礦產儲量。結果不到一個月，同個國家出現在上海的簽署桌上。
這個背景讓信件的語氣變得容易理解。中國握有關鍵礦產處理的近乎壟斷地位，並且在川普去年發動的關稅戰中已經把它當成報復工具用過一次。美國好不容易在中亞挖到一個礦產夥伴，對方轉頭就去參加了對手的成立大會。與其說這封信是最後通牒，不如說是回頭掩飾。
沒有寄往台灣
對台灣讀者來說，這件事有個容易被略過的細節。台灣不在那 35 個收件人裡面，也不在 Pax Silica 的 24 個簽署方裡面。
台灣走的是另一條管道。今年 1 月 27 日，美國在台協會（AIT）與駐美代表處（TECRO）簽署了《Pax Silica 宣言與美台經濟安全合作聯合聲明》，國務院在 6 月的峰會成果文件中特別加了一句，台灣已透過這份聯合聲明「背書 Pax Silica 宣言的原則」。6 月的華府峰會台灣也有派代表出席。
這套框架要保護的是半導體與 AI 硬體供應鏈，而那條供應鏈的物理核心就在台灣。真正需要被要求選邊的，是那些有東西可以被兩邊搶、也還有得選的國家。
常見問題
Pax Silica 是什麼？有哪些國家加入？
Pax Silica 是美國國務院 2025 年 12 月由次卿 Jacob Helberg 發起的 AI 與供應鏈安全計畫，涵蓋關鍵礦產、能源、半導體與 AI 基礎設施。今年 6 月峰會後共 24 個簽署方，包含日本、韓國、印度、澳洲、歐盟與哈薩克。
WAICO 和 Pax Silica 有什麼差別？
WAICO 是中國主導、7 月 16 日在上海成立的世界人工智慧合作組織，29 個創始成員多為全球南方國家，主打開放權重模型與 AI 培訓。Pax Silica 則以供應鏈與出口管制為核心，成員可取得共同投資機會。兩張名單目前只有哈薩克重疊。

title: 川普：打贏伊朗後把荷姆茲海峽劃成「美國領土」，絕不對開戰道歉
summary:
美國總統川普週五（8/14）在紐約長島演講時說，等打贏伊朗之後，他要把荷姆茲海峽宣布成美國領土，並強調絕對不會 […]

〈川普：打贏伊朗後把荷姆茲海峽劃成「美國領土」，絕不對開戰道歉〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
美國總統川普週五（8/14）在紐約長島演講時說，等打贏伊朗之後，他要把荷姆茲海峽宣布成美國領土，並強調絕對不會為攻打伊朗道歉，要美國人為汽油多付點錢也值得。布蘭特原油本週一度逼近 90 美元，IEA 警告全球庫存緩衝正在快速耗盡。
（前情提要：伊朗拋六大條件：美國撤軍、賠款、解凍資產，全接受才重開荷姆茲海峽）
（背景補充：美債逼近 40 兆美元大關！高息環境推升殖利率創 2007 年來新高，比特幣避險光環褪色？）
美國總統川普週五（8/14）在紐約 Garden City 的 Nassau 郡警察學院演講時丟出一句話：等打贏伊朗，他要把荷姆茲海峽宣布成美國領土。
原話是「After we finish defeating Iran, which is being very badly defeated, pretty soon I’ll be declaring the Hormuz Strait a territory of the United States」，講完他自己補了一句「It’s true」，還笑了一下。現場沒人分得出他是認真的，還是隨口說的。
這條水道戰前每天有 130 艘以上的船行經，扛著全球約五分之一的石油與液化天然氣。2 月 28 日美以對伊朗開戰後，現在每天只剩 2 到 9 艘。
同場演講川普也將油價算給選民聽，他說絕對不會為攻打伊朗道歉，要美國人為汽油「多付一點點」，換來的是一個「非常邪惡的國家」拿不到核武。他還形容對伊朗的封鎖「擋不住，那是一道鋼鐵之牆」。
美國汽油價格目前約每加侖 4 美元，布蘭特原油週三一度逼近 90 美元，週五收在 87 美元附近，單週漲了近 5%。所謂「多付一點點」，是半年疊上來的價。
伊朗的回應很快，副外長 Kazem Gharibabadi 回應「荷姆茲海峽不是一則推文能拿走的，也不是一艘航空母艦、一紙命令或一場競選演說能拿走的。伊朗不怕威脅，也不會被武力展示嚇到。」
川普不是第一次對這條水道提出主權級的構想。7 月他曾說美國可以當海峽的「守護者」，對過境貨物抽 20% 費用，後來改口取消，換成海灣國家「海量投資美國」。
庫存緩衝正在燒完
國際能源總署（IEA）8 月 12 日的月報把問題講得更硬。7 月底全球可觀測石油庫存跌破 79 億桶，是 2025 年 4 月以來首見，光 7 月單月就少掉 6,900 萬桶。從 2 月底到 7 月底，累計去庫 4.1 億桶，平均每天 270 萬桶被燒掉。
IEA 把未來幾個月的供給缺口上修到每天 180 萬桶，是 7 月估值的兩倍以上，並直接寫下重開海峽的急迫性正在升高，因為原本可用的庫存緩衝正在快速耗盡。今年全球石油供給預估減少 430 萬桶（約 4%），波灣還有每日 830 萬桶產能停擺。OPEC 的看法相反，仍預估今年需求成長 58 萬桶。一邊說庫存要見底，一邊說需求還在長，市場現在同時聽兩套數字。
代價也寫在船上。「亞伯拉罕·林肯」號航母 2025 年 11 月從聖地牙哥出港，至今部署超過 250 天，超過 200 天沒有靠港，是現代紀錄。8 月 3 日一名航空聯隊的水兵在惡劣海象中落海，穿著救生衣、一小時內被搜救直升機救起，沒有受傷，海軍把這起事件歸類為「心理健康事件」。今年 4 月，同一打擊群的驅逐艦 USS Frank E. Petersen 也發生過水兵落海。
家屬向媒體描述的艙內狀況包括發黴的淋浴間、壞掉的馬桶、好幾週沒有熱水，以及一餐只有半杯米飯配兩張墨西哥薄餅。參議員 Richard Blumenthal 與眾議員 Mike Levin 已要求國防部長 Pete Hegseth 說明。「喬治·華盛頓」號航母打擊群 8 月 5 日結束越南停靠，正前往中東接替林肯號。航母在海上撐了 250 天，總統在陸地上說封鎖是一道鋼鐵之牆。

title: 輝達揭露 SpaceX 持股 210 億鎂，投 xAI 的 100 億已經翻倍
summary:
輝達（NVIDIA）週五（8/14）向美國證券交易委員會（SEC）遞交 13F 申報，首度揭露持有 Space […]

〈輝達揭露 SpaceX 持股 210 億鎂，投 xAI 的 100 億已經翻倍〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
輝達（NVIDIA）週五（8/14）向美國證券交易委員會（SEC）遞交 13F 申報，首度揭露持有 SpaceX 的 1.228 億股 A 類普通股，截至 6 月 30 日帳面價值約 210 億美元，是它第二大公開持股。這批股票來自今年 1 月投入 xAI 的 100 億美元，2 月 SpaceX 以 1.25 兆美元吃下 xAI，投資順勢換成火箭公司的股權。但 SpaceX 上市後股價回落，這筆持股現值只剩約 172 億美元。
（前情提要：馬斯克：5 年後 AI 佔 SpaceX 估值 99%）
（背景補充：陳立武放狠話：英特爾錯過三次浪潮，這次一定讓 intel 翻盤）
重點摘要
- 輝達持有 SpaceX 1.228 億股，6 月底帳面 210 億美元，僅次於英特爾
- Intel、xAI 兩筆共 150 億美元本金，季末滾成 510 億，帳面翻 3.4 倍
- SPCX 從季末 170.86 跌到 140 美元，兩筆持股兩個月吐回 118 億美元
標籤：輝達,SpaceX,xAI,Intel,馬斯克
輝達週五向 SEC 遞交的 13F 申報顯示，它手上有 122,764,805 股 SpaceX A 類普通股，以 6 月 30 日收盤價 170.86 美元計算，帳面約 209.8 億美元。這是輝達第二大公開持股，排在英特爾（Intel）後面。
比較有意思的是這批股票怎麼來的。輝達今年 1 月參與 xAI 的 200 億美元融資輪，自己投了 100 億美元。2 月 SpaceX 以 1.25 兆美元的作價收購 xAI，輝達手上的 xAI 股權就換成了 SpaceX 股票。半年時間，100 億美元的本金在帳上變成 210 億美元。
要注意的是，這 100 億美元的數字來自知情人士向 CNBC 透露，輝達與 xAI 都沒有正式公布過交易確切規模。
按 FactSet 的資料，輝達是 SpaceX 第六大股東。馬斯克（Elon Musk）自己以 48.4% 的持股遙遙領先，市值約 8,500 億美元；Alphabet 排第二，約 780 億美元，那筆持股可以追到 2015 年 1 月的 9 億美元投資，當時 SpaceX 估值 120 億美元。同批 13F 裡，Fidelity 揭露 3.026 億股，Gigafund 1.718 億股，超微（AMD）也有近 330 萬股、約 5.65 億美元。
Intel 那筆才是真正金雞母
如果只看倍數，輝達壓在英特爾身上的錢賺得更兇。輝達去年 9 月談定、12 月完成的英特爾投資，用每股 23.28 美元吃下 2.148 億股，本金正好 50 億美元。到 6 月 30 日，這批股票帳面已經是 299.9 億美元，一年不到翻了 6 倍。
兩筆加起來，輝達拿 150 億美元的現金換到季末 510 億美元的帳面價值。同一份 13F 裡，輝達整個公開股票組合 8 檔標的、總值 634.4 億美元，光是這兩筆就佔掉八成：
- Intel: 2.148 億股, 299.9 億美元
- SpaceX A 類: 1.228 億股, 209.8 億美元
- CoreWeave: 4,721 萬股, 47.0 億美元
- Coherent: 779 萬股, 30.7 億美元
- Nokia ADR: 1.664 億股, 22.1 億美元
- Synopsys: 482 萬股, 21.5 億美元
- Nebius: 119 萬股, 3.3 億美元
- Generate Biomedicines: 83 萬股, 0.14 億美元
13F 是季末快照
這份申報的數字全部停在 6 月 30 日，而過去六週兩檔股票都在往下走。SpaceX 6 月 12 日以每股 135 美元登上那斯達克，首日收在 160.95 美元，7 月中一度跌到 108.27 美元，週五收 140 美元。單這一項，輝達帳面就從 209.8 億美元縮到約 171.9 億美元，蒸發 37.9 億美元。
英特爾股價縮水更多，CNBC 指出該持股目前約 220 億美元，比季末的 299.9 億美元少了近 80 億。兩筆合計，輝達的帳面在兩個多月內回吐約 118 億美元。
季報揭露不是現況，同批 13F 讓外界看到 Alphabet 帳上 942 億美元的 SpaceX 持股，換成週五的收盤價其實是 772 億，兩個數字差了 170 億美元。
投資與訂單綁再一起
錢投出去之後，供應關係跟著收緊。馬斯克在本月稍早 SpaceX 首份財報電話會議上說，公司的 AI 資料中心將獨家採用輝達晶片，理由是輝達 GPU 在訓練與推論上有「最好的架構」，他還說預期 SpaceX 明年能拿到 Vera Rubin GPU 的「大量配額」。SpaceX 同時把算力目標從目前的 2GW 拉到 2027 年底接近 10GW。
這個模式在輝達的投資清單上很眼熟。CoreWeave 是輝達投資的雲端業者，也是輝達 GPU 的大買家；輝達今年 1 月又追加 20 億美元幫它擴 5GW 算力。市場對這種「左手投資、右手訂單」（circular financing）的質疑一直沒斷，輝達執行長黃仁勳（Jensen Huang）則反覆否認，說這些單純就是好投資。
常見問題
輝達為什麼會持有 SpaceX 股票？
輝達今年 1 月參與 xAI 的 200 億美元融資輪，投入約 100 億美元。2 月 SpaceX 以 1.25 兆美元收購 xAI，輝達持有的 xAI 股權隨之換成 1.228 億股 SpaceX A 類普通股。
13F 申報是什麼？為什麼要看它？
13F 是管理逾 1 億美元美股資產的機構每季必須向 SEC 申報的持倉清單，於季末後 45 天內提交。它揭露的是季末當天的持股與市值快照，不反映申報日的最新價格。

title: 比特幣6.3萬鎂關口震盪！全網爆倉1.66億，美股自高點回落
summary:
比特幣今（15）日於 63,000 美元震盪整理，24 小時微跌 0.8%，以太幣報 1,882 美元。全網爆 […]

〈比特幣6.3萬鎂關口震盪！全網爆倉1.66億，美股自高點回落〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
比特幣今（15）日於 63,000 美元震盪整理，24 小時微跌 0.8%，以太幣報 1,882 美元。全網爆倉 1.66 億美元，恐慌指數回升至 34 脫離低點。上週五美股自歷史高點回落，加密市場缺乏獨立催化劑。
（前情提要：週末幣價》BTC 卡 6.4 萬鎂關口！恐懼指數 25 極度恐慌，美股 AI 晶片崩盤、原油飆漲）
（背景補充：美股大漲比特幣無感？盤整6.3萬鎂、以太坊回落1851美元，爆倉2.4億鎂恐慌指數回落）
比特幣今（15）日延續弱勢震盪格局，亞洲早盤報 63,016 美元，24 小時微跌 0.8%。以太幣同步承壓報 1,882 美元，跌幅 0.3%。受上週五美股自歷史高點小幅回落影響，加密市場整體交投清淡，全網合計爆倉 1.66 億美元，恐慌與貪婪指數回升至 34，脫離近 8 日低點。
全網爆倉 1.66 億美元，多頭失血佔六成
CoinGlass 資料顯示，過去 24 小時全網爆倉總額達 1.66 億美元，其中多單爆倉 9,729 萬美元、空單 6,864 萬美元，多頭失血佔比約 58.6%。共有 88,535 名交易者遭清算，最大單筆爆倉發生在幣安 SNDKUSDT 合約，金額 205 萬美元。
加密市場缺乏催化劑
美股上週五自歷史高點小幅回檔，標普 500 指數收跌 0.2%，道瓊工業指數跌 0.2%，那斯達克指數跌 0.3%。此前一日標普 500 甫創收盤新高，受溫和生產者物價指數（PPI）及市場對聯準會 9 月暫停升息的預期推動。然而週五公布的經濟資料意外疲弱，促使獲利了結賣壓出籠。加密資產缺乏獨立催化劑，走勢隨風險資產同步震盪。
主流幣普遍承壓，SOL、XRP 跌幅擴大
其他主流幣種同步走弱，SOL 報 75.37 美元，24 小時下跌 0.89%；XRP 報 1.0008 美元，跌幅 1.14% 相對較重。比特幣近 14 日高點為 8 月 10 日的 65,234 美元，低點則落在 8 月 3 日的 62,456 美元；以太幣同期高點為 8 月 7 日的 1,928 美元，低點為 8 月 2 日的 1,835 美元。
技術面：BTC 偏弱守布林下軌，ETH 中性區間整理
比特幣以昨日收盤價 63,044 美元計，RSI14 報 42.8 處於偏弱區域，價格已跌破 SMA20（64,005）與 SMA50（63,507），遠低於 SMA200（69,543）。
MACD 呈空頭排列，柱狀體較前一日擴大，顯示動能持續轉弱。布林通道中，收盤價貼近下軌 62,561，短期下方支撐位依序為布林下軌 62,561 與 30 日低點 62,275；上方壓力位則為 SMA50 63,507 與 SMA20 64,005。
以太幣收盤 1,882 美元，RSI14 報 51.0 處於中性區域，收盤價位於 SMA20（1,894）之下但在 SMA50（1,826）之上，均線排列多空分歧。MACD 亦呈空頭排列，但柱狀體較前一日收斂，動能減弱。布林通道中價格位於中軌 1,894 之下、下軌 1,843 之上。下方支撐位為布林下軌 1,843 與 SMA50 1,826；上方壓力位為 SMA20 1,894 與布林上軌 1,945。
恐慌指數回升至 34
Alternative.me 資料顯示，今日恐慌與貪婪指數報 34（恐懼），較前一日 29 回升 5 個百分點，終止連續數日的下滑趨勢。近 8 日指數區間落在 27 至 34，整體仍處於恐懼區間，反映市場對短期走勢態度審慎。加密貨幣市場短期缺乏明確利多催化，持續關注本週總經資料及聯準會官員談話對風險資產的影響。

title: HRW says US civil rights enforcement reduced under Trump: What to know
summary: A new report documents how federal agencies have reduced the number of civil rights cases they pursue as staffing falls.
full_text:
HRW says US civil rights enforcement reduced under Trump: What to know
A new report documents how federal agencies have reduced the number of civil rights cases they pursue as staffing falls.
According to a new report, the United States federal government has taken a massive step back from its role in protecting civil rights across the country.
On Thursday, the nonprofit Human Rights Watch issued a 112-page analysis of the government’s civil rights activities from January 2025 through the start of 2026, a period that captures the opening months of President Donald Trump’s second term.

The report concludes that the federal agencies responsible for stopping discrimination have largely been gutted of their staff.
Additionally, top-down directives by Trump have de-emphasised the federal government’s role in protecting civil rights across the country, according to the group.
“While claiming to protect all Americans, the administration is rolling back systems that communities have long turned to for relief,” Trey Walk, a researcher at Human Rights Watch, said in a statement.
Which agencies did the report analyse?
The report examines four key agencies within the federal government dedicated to civil rights.
They include the Civil Rights Division at the Department of Justice, the Office of Civil Rights at the Education Department, the Fair Housing Office at the Department of Housing and Urban Development, and the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission.
Human Rights Watch spoke with current and former federal workers, lawyers, complainants and community groups who had been involved in cases alleging discrimination.
It also reviewed court filings and federal agency directives that illustrated the pivot in priorities under the second Trump administration.
What is the history of civil rights enforcement in the federal government?
The federal government’s role in civil rights protections goes back centuries, starting with the US Constitution.
In 1791, Congress ratified an addition to the country’s founding document that established civil protections like the freedom of religion. Those first 10 amendments became known as the Bill of Rights.
Over the decades, more amendments were added, most notably after the US Civil War, to guarantee rights like equal protection under the law.
While the Constitution contains explicit language about religion and race, critics point out that there is no language that confers equal protection based on sex or gender.
The history of the Department of Justice is closely entwined with the need to enforce civil rights law after the Civil War.
Created in 1870, the department addressed several needs, including a push to professionalise and centralise the country’s federal law enforcement. But it also helped prosecute violent white supremacist groups at a time when local authorities, particularly in southern states, sometimes refused to.
The US Civil Rights Movement, starting in the 1950s, also spurred a surge in federal infrastructure. It was the Civil Rights Act of 1957, for instance, that established a dedicated civil rights division within the Justice Department.
How did federal policy change under Trump?
Trump’s second term ushered in a backlash towards policies broadly considered to be part of the “diversity, equity and inclusion” movement, or DEI.
That movement gained popularity in the early 2020s, particularly after the murder of George Floyd, an unarmed Black man, sparked a public reckoning over racial inequality.
Trump, however, has called DEI “racially discriminatory”. During his campaign for a second term, he argued that there was a “definite anti-white feeling in this country”.
Since starting his second term, Trump has sought to undo policies that his administration argues give unfair advantages to demographics like women and minorities.
In addition, federal agencies like the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission and the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division suspended certain cases they were pursuing, including some involving sexual harassment and transgender rights.
New investigations were opened instead, including against the footwear giant Nike, which was accused this year of discrimination against white employees.
In May 2025, the Department of Justice also announced it would halt investigations and reform agreements involving police departments accused of racial discrimination.
Such measures had been taken in places like Louisville, Kentucky, and Minneapolis, Minnesota, after public outcry over the police killings of unarmed Black people, including Floyd.
What did the Human Rights Watch report find?
The report chronicled an overall weakening in the federal bodies designed to protect civil rights.
Job cuts and resignations were part of that trend. The Civil Rights Division at the Department of Justice, for instance, boasted about 365 lawyers in January 2025, when Trump took office.
By the end of that year, three-quarters of those lawyers had left the agency, an exodus driven by what Human Rights Watch called a “coordinated effort to undermine career staff”.
A spokesperson for the Justice Department told Al Jazeera its Civil Rights Division “remains dedicated to protecting the rights of all Americans”.
The department also said it had added 100 personnel since the 2025 departures.
According to the spokesperson, the Civil Rights Division is currently focused on “protecting religious liberty, Second Amendment rights, and women’s and girls’ spaces, standing against illegal race-based policymaking and DEI, and defending parents’ fundamental right to direct their children’s upbringing and education”.
What other offices were affected?
Other agencies in the Human Rights Watch report likewise saw a decrease in their ranks as well as a reduction in their civil rights work.
The Office of Fair Housing went from 31 staffers to 11 by mid-2025. Some 115 complaints prepared by the office and referred to the Justice Department for possible legal action were quashed, according to the report.
At the Department of Education, the Office for Civil Rights initially had 568 workers across 12 offices when Trump took office in 2025. Within a few months, seven of those offices were shuttered, and half of the civil rights-related workers were gone.
Between May and September 2025, the office dismissed about 90 percent of the nearly 10,000 complaints it received, a higher rate than it would have in the past, the report said.
What has been the impact of these changes?
Human Rights Watch found that many victims and communities grappling with discrimination no longer had the benefit of a federal agency to help them in their cases.
One community housing group told Human Rights Watch that the Department of Housing and Urban Development no longer responds in a timely fashion to reported instances of anti-LGBTQ discrimination.
Some federal agencies also appear to have walked away from their role in monitoring discrimination and overseeing reforms around the country, according to the report.
The Department of Education’s Office of Civil Rights has a long history of investigating discrimination claims and working with school districts to enact change.
But Human Rights Watch observed that the office has largely stopped dealing with complaints under Trump.
While the Office of Civil Rights required policy changes or monitoring in response to 336 cases in the first half of 2024, only 59 cases received such a remedy over a similar period in 2025.

summary:
Picture a fisherman hauling in his nets on a calm morning at sea, when his smartwatch suddenly vibrates with an alert: “Magnetic anomaly detected – possible submarine passing 500 metres below.”
Far‑fetched as it sounds, Chinese scientists have just taken a decisive step towards making that scenario real.

full_text:
Advertisement
Chinese magnetic sensor breakthrough may help smartwatch detect submarine 500 metres deep
Compact chip containing Hall-effect sensor can pick up faint magnetic fields by generating a tiny voltage without increasing noise output
2-MIN READ2-MIN
 Listen
Zhang Tongin Beijing
Picture a fisherman hauling in his nets on a calm morning at sea, when his smartwatch suddenly vibrates with an alert: “Magnetic anomaly detected – possible submarine passing 500 metres below.”
Far‑fetched as it sounds, Chinese scientists have just taken a decisive step towards making that scenario real.
A team from the Hefei Institutes of Physical Science and the Ningbo Institute of Materials Technology and Engineering, both under the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS), has created a Hall‑effect magnetic sensor so sensitive that it could, in theory, pick up the faint magnetic shadow of a steel‑hulled submarine from half a kilometre (1,640 feet) away – all within a chip no bigger than a grain of dust.
Their findings, published on July 17 in the journal Physical Review Letters, shatter a decades-old sensitivity-versus-noise trade-off that has kept everyday magnetic sensors from hearing the quietest signals.
Hall‑effect sensors are the unsung workhorses inside many everyday gadgets. Already built into smartwatches, smartphones, car wheel‑speed detectors and hospital scanners, they detect magnetic fields by generating a tiny voltage when a field is present. They are simple, cheap, fast and compact – perfect for wearables.
But until now, shrinking them and making them more sensitive came with a punishing side‑effect: more noise, much like cranking up a radio’s volume also amplifies the hiss.

title: Iran says no decision yet on a return to talks with the US
summary: FM Abbas Araghchi says Iran is working with Oman on routes, but Hormuz shipping depends on US meeting conditions.
full_text:
Iran says no decision yet on a return to talks with the US
FM Abbas Araghchi says Iran separately working with Oman on routes, but Hormuz shipping depends on US meeting conditions.
Iran is still undecided about resuming talks with the United States to end the war, amid disagreements about ceasefire violations and the future of the Strait of Hormuz.
“We have not yet made a decision to restart negotiations with the United States,” Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said in a post on Telegram on Saturday, reiterating remarks he made to Iranian news outlet Shahrara News.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items
- list 1 of 3Norway’s FM tells Al Jazeera the US war on Iran was not ‘smart’
- list 2 of 3Trump dismisses mental health concerns on USS Lincoln aircraft carrier
- list 3 of 3US President Trump says he will declare Strait of Hormuz US territory
Mediators from both Qatar and Pakistan are exchanging messages and are in contact with Iran, “but this does not mean negotiations”, he said.
Araghchi blamed the US for the return to violence following the signing of a memorandum of understanding (MoU) in Pakistan in June, and said a new path out of the conflict must be defined.
He said Iran is separately working with Oman on a technical process to establish new routes for shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, but any transit of ships is contingent on a political solution being reached.
“The routes that previously existed are no longer functional, and a new route must be defined. We are currently designing a temporary route that will become the final route in the next stages,” the minister said.
He added that “whether or not shipping traffic in the Strait of Hormuz resumes … depends on the fulfilment of other conditions that the United States must adhere to”.
Araghchi’s comments came on the same day that US President Trump said: “After we finish defeating Iran … I’ll be declaring the Hormuz Strait a territory of the United States.”
In response, Kazem Gharibabadi, Iran’s deputy foreign minister for legal and international affairs, said on X that the “Strait of Hormuz has been Iranian, is Iranian, and will remain Iranian”.
As the two sides trade remarks, control over the key waterway remains contested.
On Friday, the UAE’s Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) said that one of its ships had come under attack while transiting the Strait of Hormuz – the latest in a string of such incidents over the past weeks.
US shifting to economic pressure
Following six months of fighting that has failed to fulfil Washington and Israel’s aim of overthrowing Iran’s leaders or opening the Strait of Hormuz, the US now appears to be signalling a move towards the use of economic pressure to achieve its goals.
On Thursday, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the US will soon apply new economic measures to pressure Iran.
“It will be a combination of economic isolation the world has never seen before, and the continued blockade in the Strait of Hormuz that will keep anything from going in or out of the Iranian ports,” he said in an interview on Newsmax.
In August, the US announced steps to dismantle a web of currency exchange houses and shell companies that it said helped Iran secretly move hundreds of millions of dollars through the international financial system.
“Iran’s shadow banking system is buckling under Economic Fury, and the regime is running out of ways to move money,” Bessent said when those sanctions were announced.
This strategy is not new: Iran has faced a web of ever-tightening economic sanctions from the US and others since the revolution in 1979. Economic troubles have repeatedly led to highly destabilising protests – but none have triggered meaningful regime change.
Marc Ginsberg, a former US ambassador and White House Middle East policy adviser, told Al Jazeera that while the US has long used maximum pressure tactics, the current situation is distinct, and the White House lacks a clear strategy to resolve the standoff.
“This is sort of a game of economic chicken. Which of the two parties is going to jump off the side of the road before a collision?” he said. “I think in the end, the administration’s going to cave before the Iranian government does.”

title: Google Workspace Promo Codes: 14% Off for August 2026
summary: Boost your productivity and save with exclusive Google Workspace coupons from WIRED. Get up to 14% off plans for three months, including Starter, Standard, and Plus tiers.
full_text:
Google Workspace is that ubiquitous modern business tool that almost feels invisible. We use it every day here at WIRED, whether that's for writing first drafts of articles in Docs, analyzing data in Sheets, or sharing files in Drive. And recently, I've been using the Gemini AI implementation that's built right into these tools, which is handy in all sorts of ways.
Google Workspace grants access to all kinds of productivity features that can help streamline processes and increase communication within a team or organization. It's not free, but here's the good news: If you're looking at a Workspace account for yourself (or for your team), Google is offering discounts until the end of 2026 using one of the Google Workspace coupon codes below. You can save up to 14 percent on plans for the first three months, whether you're signing up as an individual or as a business. Either way, the Google Workspace promo code down below is what you want to use.
Save up to 14% Off These Google Workspace Promo Codes 2026
There are some notable differences between each Workspace plan – I’ll dig into them in the next section – but all three plans come with access to the full slate of Workspace apps. You get Gmail, Drive, Calendar, and Meet, of course, but even the cheapest Starter plan includes basic access to Google’s other apps, such as NotebookLM and Gemini inside the Workspace suite. If you want to save, make sure to click one of the promo codes at the top of this page to secure your discount.
What Is the Best Google Workspace Plan?
Google offers four different Workspace plans, though only three are relevant for most people. There’s Starter, Standard, and Plus, as well as Enterprise, which is only available if you contact Google’s sales team. There isn’t a minimum number of users on any of the plans, but the bottom three options (Starter, Standard, and Plus) support up to 300 users. If you need more than that, you’ll need an Enterprise plan.
Although you have access to all the apps regardless of the plan you choose, there are some important differences, particularly between the Starter and Standard plans. Both include secure storage through Google Drive, but Starter comes with 30GB per user while Standard comes with a massive 2TB per user. Plus bumps that up to 5TB per user. Across all plans, storage is in a shared pool, so each additional user adds to the total pool of storage your organization can use.
Gemini is also a big difference between Starter and Standard. Although both have access to the Gemini app, Starter only has Gemini in Gmail and Vids. Standard (and Plus) includes Gemini across the full suite, including in Docs, Sheets, Slides, Drive, Meet, and Chat.
Starter is a great option for anyone just getting started, regardless of if you’re a freelancer or a small business with a handful of employees. In addition to 30GB per user and limited access to Gemini, Starter comes with a few other limitations. It doesn’t support e-signatures in Docs, nor advanced features of Meet, such as noise cancellation. The bread and butter of Workspace is all here, though. You get a custom domain in Gmail, up to 100 participants in Meet, and the full Google suite of productivity apps.
Standard, as the name suggests, is Workspace proper, and it’s built for teams that need room to grow. That shows up most clearly in storage space, jumping from 30GB to 2TB per user. Standard basically cuts all the red tape on Starter. There aren’t any limitations on Gemini (it’s available across the full suite), Meet features like noise cancellation are available, and you can host up to 150 participants in a Meet call. Standard even comes with expanded access to NotebookLM, Google’s AI-driven note and research tool, with different chat modes and up to 20 generative audio overviews per day.
At the top of the range is Plus, which is focused on larger businesses. You don’t get any extra apps with this plan, but you do get 5TB of storage per user, along with up to 500 participants in Meet calls. The real reason to upgrade to Plus is security and admin controls, however. It includes Vault for data retention, along with LDAP access – basically a server for centralized account management, if you aren’t familiar.
Most people should use the Standard plan, not only for the large amount of storage space over Starter, but also due to the extra Gemini functionality. If you need to upgrade to Plus down the line, you can. And, more than likely, you’ll have a member of your IT team begging you to do so.
Why Teams Love Using Google Workspace Flows with Google Workspace
Google has updated Workspace a lot over the past several months, building in new functionalities via Gemini throughout the suite. But earlier this year, Google announced that it’s bringing all of those functionalities together through Workspace Flows. It’s a no-code automation tool that lets you build automatic workflows; i.e. update a Sheet when there’s a new email in Gmail from a particular address. The interesting thing about Flows, however, is that Gemini is built into it.
You can set up basic automations, which is great given how interconnected Google’s Workspace apps already are, but Flows become powerful when you throw Gems into the mix. Gems are AI agents built with Gemini, and you can create them with specific parameters.
Let me give you an example. Say you need a marketing plan, and an employee sends you a draft. You can have a workflow set up with a Gem that’s been trained on the budget, requirements, and tone of the campaign to quickly know if it can be approved or not. Or, you can create a Gem to scan your email, trained on your organization chart and role responsibilities, to notify you whenever you receive an email that has action items for you.
Flows give you a way to add a bit of context and reasoning to the often rigid constraints of simple automation systems, and it can save you a lot of time in the process. You may be able to gather customer feedback and put it into Sheets easily, for example, but Gemini can automatically sort, summarize, and categorize that feedback so you know what you should tackle first. Flows are centralized to Workspace, as well; you don’t need to install add-ons or configure anything outside of setting up your Workspace account.
Google Workspace Flows is a new tool integrated with Google Workspace. It is powered by Google’s Gemini AI and helps you get tasks done with Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Calendar and Chat. It can fix up emails, make plans, correct sheets, or write a follow up message. No apps or links are needed.

title: Europe's scorched landscapes seen from space after summer heatwaves
summary: BBC Verify examines the impact of drought and extreme heat on western European rivers, fields and mountains.
full_text:
Europe's scorched landscapes seen from space after summer heatwaves
- Published
The impact of this summer's extreme temperatures on western Europe can now be seen from space after successive heatwaves since May.
Satellite images examined by BBC Verify show shrunken glaciers, scorched areas left by wildfires, green fields turned arid and lower river levels.
And some landmarks have been affected, too. The Palace of Versailles, south of the French capital Paris, appears as an island of trees surrounded by brown fields in these images.
The EU's climate monitoring service, Copernicus, has confirmed that western Europe experienced its hottest June-to-July period on record.
The immediate cause of the heatwaves has been persistent high-pressure weather systems bringing clear, sunny skies and allowing temperatures to build, according to the Met Office.
But climate change, mainly due to the burning of fossil fuels, has been raising average temperatures for decades and making hot spells much more likely and intense.
We've taken a look at how the sweltering weather has left its mark on landscapes across the continent.
Rivers run drier
The waters of the Danube, Europe's second-longest river, have dropped to their lowest levels for 30 years in several countries.
This has led to unusual discoveries on the river bed, including the bones of a mammoth in Bulgaria and a sunken WW2 warship in Serbia. You can see the sunken ship has emerged from the deep in the right-hand image below.
And where the river snakes through Hungary and Romania, nuclear power stations have been forced to shut down or run at reduced capacity for some time because of an inability to use river water for cooling.
Meanwhile on the Rhine, some cargo vessels have been left stranded and river cruises have been cancelled.
Retreating glaciers in the Alps
Even the snow-capped peaks of the Alps have not escaped the heat.
Ongoing measurements suggest this summer could become one of the worst ever recorded for melting Alpine glaciers, with more than a month of the season still to go.
After a mild winter, glaciers had less snow cover than usual at the end of April - and an unusually early heatwave the following month accelerated the melting of snow.
This exposed the ice beneath, leaving the glaciers vulnerable to melting faster in subsequent heatwaves.
As you can see below, satellite imagery suggests much of the front of Rhône Glacier in Switzerland has retreated by 50m (160ft) or more since the same time last year.
In a stable climate, glaciers would be expected to remain more or less the same size over the long-term.
Dr Lander van Tricht, glaciologist at the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology, said in recent years climate change has led to "much less snow in winter and much, much more melt in summer.
"And if we continue this trend, then the future looks very dramatic for the Alps."
Wildfires turn landscapes brown
Wildfires have transformed parts of western Europe this summer, too.
More than 90,000 hectares (900 sq km or 350 sq miles) has burned in France. This is already its worst year on record, according to the European Forest Fire Information System.
The largest fire in Gironde region, where the city of Bordeaux is situated, burnt about 42,000 hectares of land - roughly equivalent in size to the Isle of Wight.
Part of the reason this year has been particularly bad for wildfires is that land has been tinder-dry.
Dr Douglas Kelley of the UK Centre for Ecology and Hydrology tells us extreme wildfires are becoming "more and more frequent" as climate change is creating ideal conditions, with higher temperatures drying out vegetation and soils faster.
Even zoomed-out satellite imagery of western France shows a striking increase in the browning of land compared to last year.
To assess whether 2026 is unusual we used the Normalised Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), a measure which uses satellite data to assess how green and healthy vegetation is. Lower readings indicate more sparse or stressed vegetation.
The NDVI this summer came in below a five-year benchmark of 2021 to 2025 across about 70% of France. Close to half the UK and roughly 40% of western Germany showed the same.
Prof Andrew Challinor, from the University of Leeds, said the images were "consistent with widespread water stress", which "does not bode well" given much of Europe's land is covered by crops meaning it could hit the agriculture industry and food production.
In the worst-affected areas, soil moisture is lower than on about 98% of comparable dates in the historical record, according to Prof Luis Samaniego, from the Helmholtz Centre for Environmental Research.
And, he warns, even if rain returns, some of the agricultural damage may already have been done.

Taiwan passes defence budget after record delay, retains drone funding
Taiwan’s parliament ends deadlock, ensuring vital drone programme funding amid rising cross-strait tensions with Beijing.
Taiwan’s opposition-controlled parliament has approved the government’s annual budget, preserving funding for a drone programme central to the island’s defence plans against China.
Lawmakers passed the $93bn budget late on Friday, after a record 266 days of political deadlock and its legal deadline, as President William Lai Ching-te’s administration, which lost its parliamentary majority in 2024, continues to clash with opposition parties over government spending.

list of 3 items

- list 2 of 3HRW says US civil rights enforcement reduced under Trump: What to know
- list 3 of 3US President Trump says he will declare Strait of Hormuz US territory
The approved funding was earmarked for drone development, despite an earlier threat by the main opposition party, the Kuomintang, to slash that funding by 70 percent.
The Kuomintang dropped the proposed cut after concluding there was no wasteful overlap between the development and procurement programmes it had initially cited as justification.
Other reductions included a 60 percent cut to special allowances for government agency heads, a 2.5 percent cut to military equipment and facilities spending, and a 50 percent cut to media policy and publicity budgets.
Before Friday’s vote, the government had been operating under a provisional budget mechanism to keep paying civil servants and funding welfare programmes.
Legislative Speaker Han Kuo-yu, following the vote, said the prolonged delay had caused “social division and a constitutional impasse”.
He called on both the ruling and opposition camps to seek greater compromise going forward.
Lai said in a statement that parliamentary oversight and review of the budget are an important constitutional duty.
In May, the same opposition-controlled legislature cut a proposed $40bn special defence budget by 38 percent, stripping out all funding for domestically produced combat drones and leaving only United States arms purchases intact.
Taiwan’s military currently holds fewer than 5,000 drones, while China is reported to have ordered close to a million for delivery this year, part of a broader regional buildup that includes Ukraine’s target of seven million drones in 2026.
Beijing claims self-ruled Taiwan as its own territory and has sharply escalated military pressure on the island in recent years.

title: ‘My heart breaks into a million pieces’: emotional tributes to Kumanjayi Little Baby at Alice Springs funeral
summary:
Hundreds gathered with flashes of pink to farewell the five-year-old girl, who was allegedly murdered in April

full_text:
A sombre funeral service for Kumanjayi Little Baby has been attended by hundreds of people from the Alice Springs community and surrounds.
Wearing pink and some dressed in T-shirts bearing the face of the five-year-old girl, the crowd gathered under grey skies in the red centre capital on Saturday.
Family members surrounded a small coffin adorned with flowers and cried together.
The girl’s grandfather, Robin Japanangka Granites, opened the funeral to the public to allow the community to grieve as one.
“You come because you are one of our family,” he told them.
“You are from here and we need you because we both cried at that same time.”
In a eulogy read on her behalf, Kumanjayi Little Baby’s mother, Jacinta Roy, urged that her daughter be remembered for who she was.
She was a girl who loved watching shows like Masha and the Bear and Bluey, as well as playing games on her mum’s phone, Roy said.
The young girl also loved cuddling puppies and the colour pink.
“As a mother, my heart breaks into a million pieces,” she said. “I miss her.
“As a Christian, I would like to thank Father, Son and Holy Spirit for gifting me with a beautiful, precious little baby girl for the precious time that I was her mother here on Earth.”
The family of the allegedly murdered girl invited the desert community to farewell her on Saturday while embracing her favourite colour, pink.
The service comes months after her disappearance sparked one of the largest searches in Northern Territory history.
Kumanjayi Little Baby – as she is known for cultural reasons after her death – went missing on the outskirts of Alice Springs in late April.
It prompted an intensive five-day search by emergency services and local volunteers in grassy bushland.
The discovery of her body prompted a nationwide outpouring of grief, with vigils held across the country.
A 47-year-old man is awaiting trial after being charged with her murder.
Japanangka Granites, a Warlpiri elder, thanked locals for their efforts to locate Kumanjayi Little Baby and for their support of his family.
Kumanjayi Little Baby would be with our “father in heaven”, he said at the time.

title: Concerns grow over increased global ties with Taliban in Afghanistan
summary:
Campaigners fear deeper diplomatic contacts are undermining demands for improvements in human rights

The Taliban in Afghanistan have launched a diplomatic effort to end their isolation as major regional and international powers show a readiness to engage more closely with the repressive regime despite its systematic human rights abuses.

Five years after the Taliban took power, an increasing number of countries are renewing ties or scaling up diplomatic contacts with the hardline Islamists, who seized power in Kabul in 2021 after 20 years of brutal insurgent warfare.

Continue reading...
full_text:
The Taliban in Afghanistan have launched a diplomatic effort to end their isolation as major regional and international powers show a readiness to engage more closely with the repressive regime despite its systematic human rights abuses.
Five years after the Taliban took power, an increasing number of countries are renewing ties or scaling up diplomatic contacts with the hardline Islamists, who seized power in Kabul in 2021 after 20 years of brutal insurgent warfare.
Campaigners fear that the individual contacts by different countries risk undermining “coherent, consistent” demands for an improvement in human rights in return for any diplomatic concessions.
The United Nations described a recent “cascade of [Taliban] edicts and laws” that have banned women from universities and most employment, denied teenage girls education and imposed strict dress codes. Minorities have been persecuted, while activists and journalists face repression. Afghanistan has become a “graveyard for human rights,” the UN said in March.
India, Qatar, China, Iran and several central Asian states all recently welcomed Taliban officials or opened new channels of communication. Russia, which recognised the Taliban government in Kabul just over a year ago, signed a military cooperation agreement last month. In June, the European Union held talks with Taliban officials in Brussels about returning failed asylum-seekers to Afghanistan. Individual European countries have also deepened their own contacts with Kabul.
“There is no doubt there has been an evolution. The Islamic emirate is now in a confident position. They have realised they are indispensable for regional countries right now and even with Europe and the US they have identified how to engage,” said Shivam Shekhawat, at the Observer Research Foundation in Delhi.
“The Taliban see any kind of contact as a diplomatic win and they have been able to capitalise on that as a sign granting legitimacy to the regime.”
A strict policy of isolation imposed after the Taliban seized power in 2021 towards informal or “de facto” recognition is now fragmenting. Some western commentators have suggested more countries recognise the regime. Others want intensified “back channel” engagement.
“We are not against any engagement … There is a need for engagement even if just for aid agencies to mitigate the ongoing humanitarian crisis but we are worried about the end goal of these contacts and the discussions that are taking place,” said Fereshta Abbasi, Afghanistan researcher at Human Rights Watch.
“There should be a consistent and coherent message from the international community to the Taliban that they will not have any friends if they do not show real progress in terms of the women’s rights and human rights situation … and that is not happening.”
The new contacts stem from a combination of regional security concerns, pressure in the west to reduce illegal immigration and a general recognition that the Taliban are unlikely to be forced from power in the foreseeable future.
The European Commission downplayed its discussions in Brussels with a Taliban delegation, the first such formal encounter since 2021, as merely “technical” and focused on returns, but a Taliban spokesperson claimed it was a historic visit that was a step towards regularising consular relations with EU countries.
The meeting prompted outrage.
“You cannot condemn Taliban abuses in one breath and then announce talks on immigration in the next … The Taliban are telling their constituency back home that they are now accepted by the international community,” said Abbasi.
This year officials from Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan have all visited Kabul or other Afghan cities, seeking trade routes and pipeline deals that would allow their landlocked countries access to seaports or third countries beyond.
India too has moved to reinforce relationships that were frosty after the fall of Kabul to the Taliban in 2021, in part to exploit new tensions between the movement and the Islamist movement’s historic sponsors, Pakistan.
New Delhi secured a sanctions waiver last year so that Amir Khan Muttaqi, the Taliban foreign minister and a veteran official who has spent decades at the heart of the movement, could travel there.
In June, India’s UN envoy suggested a rethink was necessary on sanctions, such as travel bans, asset freezes and arms embargoes, that target dozens of Taliban members.
“The political reality of Afghanistan has changed in the last five years, and the current UN sanctions regime must take that into account,” said Harish Parvathaneni.
Afghan authorities’ diplomatic strategy has involved hosting envoys in Kabul, including those from China, Japan, Turkey and Saudi Arabia. Last year, Iran’s foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, made the first visit by an Iranian foreign minister to Kabul for almost a decade.
The Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan “seeks relations with all countries”, Taliban spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid said, though “the countries of the region and our neighbouring states have particular importance, because our economic ties and interests are closely linked”.
Anna Borshchevskaya, a senior fellow at The Washington Institute focusing on Russia’s policy towards the Middle East, said Moscow had multiple reasons for recognising the Taliban regime and seeking closer relations.
“One likely objective is simply having allies … Afghanistan is also very significant for Russia geographically and Russia just wants influence in that part of the world. There was an opening and they were able to take it,” Borshchevskaya said.
“It’s a very cold, cynical calculation. It’s part of a very simple zero-sum view that for Russia to win the US has to lose. From the Kremlin perspective, this is a global battle and whether you are looking at Europe or Afghanistan or wherever, it’s one geopolitical chessboard.”
Britain has said it pursues a policy of “limited and pragmatic” engagement with Taliban officials, largely through the UK Mission to Afghanistan based at the British embassy in Qatar. Discreet meetings with the Taliban have also repeatedly been held by other western countries in Qatar. In Germany and at least four other western European capitals, key consulates are now controlled by the Taliban, not representatives of the former Afghan government.
Taliban officials have also sought cross-border infrastructure projects to boost the country’s fragile economy and diplomacy. Natural resources are another lure for overseas powers. Kabul has expanded the mining sector, attracting firms from neighbouring China and elsewhere.
China, which is worried about Islamic militancy on and around its south-western borders, has welcomed Taliban officials in recent years, and hosted talks when Afghanistan and Pakistan went to war earlier this year.
The Taliban are split, with deep disagreements on the ban on women’s education among other issues, but remain dominated by the most conservative factions. Recent laws have further reinforced repression, designating many religious minorities, including Shia Muslims, as heretics and imposing strict punishments to silence dissent.
Other new laws recognise only “excessive” beating as domestic violence against women and facilitate the marriage of girls without their consent. 
Analysts do not believe the Taliban are likely to moderate their position in the near future and point to the continuing authority of Hibatullah Akhundzada, the reclusive and authoritarian cleric leader.
Ramin Mansoori, a researcher at the University of Pittsburgh and Carnegie Endowment who studies Afghan politics, said the Taliban’s priority was its domestic agenda.
“They are not going to make any significant concessions. Most of them don’t have an international perspective,” Mansoori said.

title: Heathrow Airport warns of disruption following floods
summary: Water in the central terminal area means passengers cannot use roads to the airport
full_text:
Heathrow Airport warns of disruption following floods
- Published
Heathrow Airport has warned access to Terminals 2 and 3 is restricted because of flooding.
Water in the central terminal area means anyone trying to travel to or from either of these terminals cannot travel by road.
Instead passengers are being advised to travel by rail and tube and to avoid using cars.
"Our teams are working to resolve the situation as quickly as possible, we apologise for any disruption caused," the airport said early on Saturday.
The disruption comes during the school holidays, one of the busiest periods for the airport.
Heathrow said 19 July was its busiest day of the year so far as many schools broke up for summer, with 267,000 passengers passing through.
The airport was recently affected by disruption to railway services, after a water leak prompted the closure of a tunnel.
